title: A Hamilton path bounds the components of a vertex-deletion
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on vertex set $V$, and suppose $G$ has a Hamilton path, that is, a path passing through every vertex of $G$ exactly once. Then for every nonempty proper subset $S \subsetneq V$, the graph $G - S$ obtained by deleting the vertices of $S$ has at most $\abs{S} + 1$ connected components.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
G has a Hamilton path (some walk between two vertices visiting every vertex once)
S is a proper subset of V (S ≠ univ)
